After cooling, 30% aq NaOH was added dropwise to pH 10.0 and the resulting precipitate was filtered, washed several times with water and dried in vacuo to give the corresponding formyl derivative 7a-r (80-95%), which was generally used without further purification. General Procedure for the synthesis of formyl pyrroles (7a-r). Phosphorous oxychloride (0.5 mL, 6 mmol) was added dropwise to stirred ice-cooled DMF (12 mL) under a N2 atmosphere. The mixture was then allowed to warm to room temperature over 15 min, a solution of the pyrrole (6a-r) (1 mmol) in DMF (5 mL) added and the mixture heated at 100 °C for 3 h under a N2 atmosphere. After cooling, 30% aq NaOH was added dropwise to pH 10.0 and the resulting precipitate was filtered, washed several times with water and dried in vacuo to give the corresponding formyl derivative 7a-r (80-95%), which was generally used without further purification. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: A. General procedure for the microwave-accelerated synthesis of 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrroles (6). 2,5-Hexandione (4) (1 mmol), the appropriate aniline 5a-x (1.2 equiv) and p-toluenesulfonic acid bound with silica gel (0.4 equiv) were mixed in an oven dried pressure vial with a magnetic stirrer bar. The vessel was placed in a microwave oven and heated (180 °C, 15-20 min) under microwave irradiation (0-400 W at 2.45 GHz). After stirring for a further 15 min at room temperature the reaction mixture was filtered and the residual silica washed with DCM (10 mL). The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give the corresponding 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrrole 6a-x (80-90% yield, purity >95% by LCMS). 2,5-Dimethyl-1-(2-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)-1H-pyrrole (6a). Prepared following General Procedure A to give 6a. 3-(2,5-Dimethyl-1H-pyrrol-1-yl)pyridine (6r). Prepared following General Procedure A to give 6r as a dark-brown oil (2.8 g, 93%). 1H NMR (500 MHz, CDCl3): δ 8.50 (d, 1H, J = 1.5 Hz), 8.49 (d, 1H, J = 1.55 Hz), 8.38 (d, 1H, J = 2.05 Hz), 7.43 (m, 1H, J = 1.6 Hz), 5.79 (s, 2H), 1.89 (s, 6H). MS (ESI): calcd for C11H13N2, 173.1170; m/z found 173.1081 (M+1), 100%.

The obtained mixture was heated at reflux for 3-12 h until the dissapearance of diketone 7a-c as determined by TLC (eluent EtOAc). General/Typical Procedure: Typical Procedure. A mixture of 2,5-hexadione (570 mg, 5 mmol), aniline (558 mg, 6 mmol), and amberlite IR 120 (200 mg) was stirred at room temperature under solvent-free conditions for 18 min. After completion of reaction, as monitered by thin-layer chromatography (TLC), the reaction mixture was diluted with diethyl ether and filtered to recover the catalyst. The ether layer was washed with saturated sodium bicarbonate solution and brine solution, dried (anhydrous Na2SO4), and concentrated in vacuo. The recovered catalyst was washed with 5% diluted HCl and dried prior to reuse. The IR spectrum of the recovered catalyst was identical to that of the commercially available catalyst, which was reused for further reactions (six times) without loss of activity.
